title.narrative: Sustainable Livestock Production to Support Resilient Food Systems, Environment and Rural Livelihoods in Indonesia

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

Socio-economic benefitsThe simultaneous and synergistic generation of environmental and socio-economic benefits is fundamental to the logic of the project, as set out in Section B: the project will support the Government of Indonesia in delivering on its goals in relation to socioeconomic development, food security and nutrition in ways that are environmentally sustainable and that therefore do not undermine the condition of the natural resources on which their productive sustainability depends.The specific focus of the project on supporting the integration of environmentally sustainable livestock development practices into diversified and well managed farming, livelihood and landscape systems, rather than solely addressing issues of production, will help to ensure that beneficiaries’ livelihoods are resilient to climatic and economic shocks and trends, and that all members of farm families (including women and youth) have reliable and equitable access to on- and off-farm income, diverse farm goods and products, and nutrition. The results framework provides for specific gender-sensitive indicators to track income and nutrition benefits, as well as levels of engagement in governance and planning processes. Decent rural employmentThe project will promote decent rural employment by specifically focusing on the following entry points: Pillar 1 Employment creation and enterprise development Pillar 2 Social protection Pillar 3 Standards and rights at work Pillar 4 Governance and social dialogue • Supporting women and men small-scale producers in accessing markets and modern value chains for livestock products • Supporting agribusiness and marketing micro, small and medium enterprises in accessing markets, training, financial services and other productive assets[1] • Training programmes on technical and business skills for rural people • Support to employment-centred livelihood diversification • Supporting livestock sector enterprises that incorporate occupational safety and health measures and provide for improved working conditions • Supporting labour-saving technologies for rural poor households to reduce women’s domestic and care tasks, such as household biogas[2] • Supporting socially responsible livestock production systems that provide opportunities for women and youth • Supporting the avoidance of child labour by tackling its root causes (e.g. poverty) and providing livelihood alternatives to poor households • Supporting livestock sector enterprises that comply with national labour legislation • Strengthening organizations and networks of producers and workers, particularly in the informal rural food economy • Supporting the representation of the rural poor in social and policy dialogue through their organizations • Supporting the participation of people living in poverty in local decision-making and governance mechanisms[3], including the empowerment of rural women and youth • Building synergies and co-learning between organizations, programmes, countries and producers [1] As mentioned in the GAP, the project will build on or adapt methodologies including Farm Business Schools or Women’s Empowerment Farmer Business Schools (see Promoting gender-sensitive farm business schools. A companion guide and Women’s empowerment farmer business schools foster gender balance for household & community benefits) [2] FAO has developed toolkits for gender sensitive social protection within the FIRST programme: Gender-sensitive social protection [3] For example Dimitra Clubs
to catalyze the transformation of livestock systems in Indonesia for increased self-sufficiency, sustainability, and the delivery of multiple global environmental benefits (GEBs).
